visual.general_description: Two axial post-contrast brain MRI slices side by side, one with numerous small bright foci and one without.
visual.detailed_description: Two grayscale axial brain MRI slices sit side by side on a black background, separated by a white vertical divider. The image-left slice shows many small discrete bright dot-like foci scattered through the white matter of both hemispheres, denser in the posterior half, with a few larger or clustered bright foci near the posterior ventricular region and around the image-right side; a bright rim outlines the scalp and a bright band marks the posterior midline. The image-right slice, at a similar axial level, shows a dark brain parenchyma with no discrete bright foci; only the scalp and skull rim, a bright band along its image-right outer edge and the posterior midline are bright, with thin curvilinear lines near the ventricles. No letters, arrows, text, scale or annotations are visible.

caption_claims.value: Axial post-contrast MRI before and after treatment: enhancing nodules disappeared, meningeal enhancement improved, residual hyperintense T2 foci and possible susceptibility-weighted hypointense foci in the posterior periventricular region

evidence.quote: Axial views of post-contrast MRI show the difference between before (right) and after (left) treatment. The enhancing nodules have dramatically disappeared, indicating significant improvement. The previously seen meningeal enhancement is also improved, with several residual hyperintense T2 foci in the posterior periventricular region. There is also a suggestion of several tiny susceptibility-weighted imaging hypointense foci in the posterior periventricular region (sites of previous nodules), which may represent areas of calcification. This could be confirmed by a follow-up brain CT.

clinical_significance.statement: The authors present the pair as before and after treatment, stating the enhancing nodules dramatically disappeared and meningeal enhancement improved.

evidence.quote: The enhancing nodules have dramatically disappeared, indicating significant improvement.

limitations: T2 and susceptibility-weighted sequences named in the caption cannot be identified in these post-contrast images; residual T2 foci and possible calcification are caption claims only.
